title: Comparison & Boolean Expressions
objective: Write comparisons and combine them with and/or/not to form Boolean expressions.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Comparison and Boolean operators taught ahead of if statements as their own building block. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A comparison asks a yes-or-no question about two values and produces True or False. == checks equality, != checks inequality, and <, >, <=, >= compare size. A single = assigns a value; a double == compares two values — mixing them up is one of the most common early bugs.
True and False are Python's Boolean values — there are only ever these two, and every comparison produces one of them.

You can combine comparisons with and, or, and not. and is True only when both sides are True. or is True when at least one side is True. not flips a Boolean's value, turning True into False and back again.
explanation.rule: == compares two values for equality; = assigns a value to a variable. They are never interchangeable.

examples.title: Combining Conditions
examples.code:
temperature = 1250
is_hot_enough = temperature >= 1200
is_too_hot = temperature > 1500

print(is_hot_enough and not is_too_hot)
examples.note: The forge is ready when it's hot enough but not dangerously hot — True in this case.

checks.question: What does score == 10 do?
options: Checks whether score currently equals 10 and produces True or False.

feedback.incorrect: A single = assigns; a double == compares. score == 10 only checks the current value.

assignment.title: Ready to Forge
assignment.brief: Write is_ready(temperature) that prints True if temperature is at least 1200 and at most 1500, otherwise prints False, using and.
assignment.starterCode:
def is_ready(temperature):
    # Combine two comparisons with 'and' and print the result.
    pass

is_ready(1300)
assignment.solutionCode:
def is_ready(temperature):
    ready = temperature >= 1200 and temperature <= 1500
    print(ready)

is_ready(1300)
assignment.testHarness:
# ---- Code Forge validation ----
import io, contextlib
_cf_buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(_cf_buf):
    is_ready(1300)
_cf_result = _cf_buf.getvalue()
print("__CF_TEST_OUTPUT__")
print(repr(_cf_result))

hints: You need two comparisons joined by and.
temperature >= 1200 checks the lower bound; temperature <= 1500 checks the upper bound.
Store the combined Boolean in a variable, then print it.
print() will show True or False exactly as Python capitalizes them.
